items.stem:
DOCUMENT-BASED QUESTION: The Marshall Plan — Economic Aid as Cold War Strategy

Directions: Read the following two primary source excerpts and then respond to the prompt below. Analyze both documents using the SOAPS framework (Speaker, Occasion, Audience, Purpose, Significance) and construct an evidence-based argument.

---
DOCUMENT A: Secretary of State George C. Marshall, Commencement Address at Harvard University, June 5, 1947 — U.S. government document, available through the Avalon Project, Yale Law School:
"It is logical that the United States should do whatever it is able to do to assist in the return of normal economic health in the world, without which there can be no political stability and no assured peace. Our policy is directed not against any country or doctrine but against hunger, poverty, desperation, and chaos. Any government that is willing to assist in the task of recovery will find full co-operation... on the part of the United States Government. Any government which maneuvers to block the recovery of other countries cannot expect help from us."

DOCUMENT B: Soviet Foreign Minister Vyacheslav Molotov, Statement rejecting the Marshall Plan, Paris Conference, July 2, 1947 — diplomatic record, available through the Avalon Project, Yale Law School:
"The American plan splits Europe into two groups of states and creates new difficulties in the relations between them... The Marshall plan, which envisages for American credits various conditions infringing on the sovereignty of European countries and interfering in their home affairs... will lead to nothing but a further aggravation of relations between countries."

---
Using both documents and your knowledge of Cold War economic competition (US.61, US.59), construct an argument that evaluates the Marshall Plan as a Cold War strategic instrument. Apply SOAPS analysis to both documents and address: (1) whether Marshall's stated humanitarian purpose was consistent with the Plan's actual geopolitical effects; (2) why the Soviet Union rejected the Plan and whether that rejection was strategically rational; and (3) what the exchange between these two documents reveals about the fundamental incompatibility that defined the early Cold War.
items.stemEs:
PREGUNTA BASADA EN DOCUMENTOS: El Plan Marshall — Ayuda Económica como Estrategia de la Guerra Fría

Instrucciones: Lee los siguientes dos fragmentos de fuentes primarias y responde al indicador a continuación. Analiza ambos documentos usando el marco SOAPS (Orador, Ocasión, Audiencia, Propósito, Significado).

DOCUMENTO A: Secretario de Estado George C. Marshall, Discurso de Graduación en la Universidad de Harvard, 5 de junio de 1947.
"Es lógico que los Estados Unidos hagan todo lo que puedan para ayudar al retorno de la salud económica normal en el mundo, sin la cual no puede haber estabilidad política ni paz asegurada..."

DOCUMENTO B: Ministro de Relaciones Exteriores Soviético Vyacheslav Molotov, Declaración rechazando el Plan Marshall, Conferencia de París, 2 de julio de 1947.
"El plan americano divide a Europa en dos grupos de estados y crea nuevas dificultades en las relaciones entre ellos..."

Usando ambos documentos y tu conocimiento de la competencia económica de la Guerra Fría (US.61, US.59), construye un argumento que evalúe el Plan Marshall como instrumento estratégico de la Guerra Fría.
